questions.question: As per the NITI Aayog Report titled 'FAST TRACKING FREIGHT IN INDIA' of 2021, what was the share of road transport in the freight traffic?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0.71**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• According to the NITI Aayog report titled **'FAST TRACKING FREIGHT IN INDIA' (2021)**, the road transport sector accounted for **71% of the freight traffic in India**.
 
• This dominance of road transport is attributed to its flexibility, last-mile connectivity, and the rapid growth of e-commerce and logistics sectors.
 
• The share of railways in freight transport was significantly lower, emphasizing the need for a modal shift to reduce logistics costs and environmental impact.
 
• The report highlights the need for **improving multi-modal logistics** and enhancing the efficiency of rail, waterways, and air transport systems.
 
• With freight transport demand expected to grow rapidly, **road transport's share must be complemented by increased investment in sustainable alternatives**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Freight Transport in India:**

 
 
• India's freight transport is dominated by roadways, followed by railways, inland waterways, and air transport.
 
• Freight traffic demand is expected to grow at a CAGR of 5.9% between 2020 and 2050, as per NITI Aayog estimates.
 
 
 
• **Challenges in Road Freight Transport:**
 
 
• High logistics costs: India's logistics costs are 13-14% of GDP, higher than developed countries' average of 8-10%.
 
• Environmental concerns: Road transport contributes significantly to greenhouse gas emissions and air pollution.
 
• Infrastructure bottlenecks: Lack of proper road infrastructure and congestion affect transport efficiency.
 
 
 
• **Proposed Solutions:**
 
 
• Shifting freight to rail and waterways to reduce costs and environmental impact.
 
• Development of multi-modal logistics parks to enhance connectivity and reduce transit times.
 
• Use of technology for efficient freight tracking and reduced delays.
 
 
 
• **Government Initiatives:**
 
 
• The Bharatmala Pariyojana aims to improve road infrastructure and connectivity across the country.
 
• The Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) project aims to enhance the efficiency and capacity of rail freight transport.
 
• Promotion of electric and alternative fuel vehicles to reduce the carbon footprint of road transport.

questions.question: Who is responsible for preparing the inaugural speech of the President of India in Indian Parliament?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The inaugural speech of the President of India in Parliament is prepared by **The Council of Ministers**, which advises the President on the content of the address.
 
• It is presented at the beginning of the first session of each year or after the formation of a new government.
 
• The speech outlines the government's policies, priorities, and legislative agenda for the upcoming year.
 
• This address is a constitutional requirement under **Article 87 of the Indian Constitution**.
 
• It serves as a medium for the government to communicate its vision and plans to the Parliament and the nation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Article 87 of the Indian Constitution:**

 
 
• It mandates the President to address both Houses of Parliament at the commencement of the first session each year.
 
• The speech is designed to inform the legislature about the government's policies and agenda.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Council of Ministers:**
 
 
• The Council of Ministers, headed by the Prime Minister, assists the President in drafting the speech.
 
• This ensures that the address reflects the collective policy decisions and priorities of the government.
 
 
 
• **Importance of the Presidential Address:**
 
 
• It sets the tone for parliamentary discussions and debates for the upcoming session.
 
• The address acts as a bridge between the executive branch and the legislative branch of the government.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• The tradition of the Presidential Address was inherited from the British parliamentary system.
 
• It underscores the ceremonial significance of the President's role in India's constitutional framework.

questions.question: What was the name of India's humanitarian mission to provide assistance to Myanmar after the earthquake in March 2025?

__
 
• **Operation Brahma** was India's humanitarian mission initiated to provide emergency relief to Myanmar following a devastating earthquake in March 2025.
 
• The operation aimed to deliver medical aid, food supplies, and search-and-rescue teams to affected regions of Myanmar.
 
• The mission was coordinated by the **National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA)** of India in collaboration with Myanmar's government.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)**

 
 
• NDRF is a specialized force under the Ministry of Home Affairs in India, tasked with handling natural and human-made disasters.
 
• The force is equipped with advanced equipment and trained personnel for disaster management and rescue operations.
 
• NDRF played a pivotal role during Operation Brahma in Myanmar by conducting rescue missions and delivering relief materials.

• India's foreign policy emphasizes strengthening relations with neighboring countries through cooperation and mutual assistance.
 
• Under this policy, India provides humanitarian aid and disaster relief to neighboring nations during crises.
 
• Operation Brahma was a prime example of India's commitment to this policy.
 
 
 
• **Earthquake Disaster Management**

• Disaster management includes rescue operations, medical support, and rehabilitation for affected populations.
 
• India's NDMA and NDRF regularly train for earthquake-related disaster response, ensuring readiness for missions like Operation Brahma.

• Such operations often include delivering food, water, medicine, and shelter to affected populations.
 
• India has conducted several humanitarian assistance missions, including Operation Brahma, showcasing its leadership in regional disaster response.

questions.question: Which of the following pairs of reform organisations and their founders is correctly matched?

options.text: Arya Samaj - Raja Ram Mohan Roy

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Satya Shodhak Samaj - Jyotiba Phule**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Satya Shodhak Samaj** was founded by Jyotiba Phule in 1873 in Pune, Maharashtra, with the aim of promoting social equality and challenging caste-based discrimination.
 
• The organization focused on uplifting marginalized sections of society, including lower castes and women, by spreading education and awareness about their rights.
 
• It opposed the dominance of the Brahminical priesthood and sought to challenge the rigid caste hierarchy prevalent in Indian society at the time.
 
• Jyotiba Phule and his wife, Savitribai Phule, actively worked to provide education to women and oppressed communities, believing that education was the key to social reform.
 
• Satya Shodhak Samaj also emphasized self-respect, rational thinking, and the rejection of blind faith and superstitions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Brahmo Samaj:**

 
 
• Founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828, it aimed at reforming Hindu society by abolishing practices like Sati and promoting widow remarriage and education for women.
 
• It advocated monotheism, rational thinking, and a departure from idol worship and rituals.
 
 
 
• **Arya Samaj:**
 
 
• Founded by Dayanand Saraswati in 1875, Arya Samaj emphasized the Vedas as the ultimate source of knowledge and guidance.
 
• It advocated social reforms such as the abolition of caste discrimination, child marriage, and untouchability.
 
 
 
• **Bahujan Samaj:**
 
 
• This term is generally associated with the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP), founded by Kanshi Ram in 1984, to represent the Dalits, Adivasis, Other Backward Classes (OBCs), and minority communities.
 
• BR Ambedkar, a key Dalit leader and social reformer, laid the ideological foundation for movements advocating the rights of marginalized communities.
 
 
 
• **Jyotiba Phule's Contributions:**
 
 
• He was a social reformer, writer, and activist who challenged the caste system and gender inequality in India.
 
• He authored several important works, including "Gulamgiri" (Slavery), which critiqued the caste system and called for equality.

__
 
• **Linux (Ubuntu, Fedora, etc.)** is an open-source operating system known for offering maximum control over system resources, making it highly suitable for professional software development.
 
• Linux is widely preferred by developers due to its **customizability**, allowing users to modify the kernel, install specific libraries, and configure the system as per their requirements.
 
• It supports a vast range of programming languages and tools, including **Python, C++, Java, Git, Docker**, and more, making it a go-to choice for software development.
 
• Popular distributions like **Ubuntu** and **Fedora** come with pre-installed development tools and have extensive community support for troubleshooting and enhancements.

• Linux distributions use package managers like **APT (for Debian/Ubuntu)** or **DNF (for Fedora)** to easily install, update, and manage software packages.

• Linux is considered more secure than many other operating systems due to its robust permission structure and active community-driven updates.
 
• It is less prone to malware and viruses, making it a reliable choice for development environments.
 
 
 
• **Server and Cloud Integration**
 
 
• Linux is extensively used in server environments, and its compatibility with cloud platforms like AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud makes it indispensable for modern software development.
 
• Many web servers (e.g., Apache, NGINX) and database systems (e.g., MySQL, PostgreSQL) are optimized for Linux.

questions.question: An astronomical observation site, Jantar Mantar, which is also a UNESCO World Heritage Site, is located in which State?​
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Jantar Mantar** is located in Jaipur, Rajasthan, and is recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
• This astronomical observation site was built by Maharaja **Sawai Jai Singh II** in the early 18th century (1727–1734).
 
• It consists of a collection of **19 architectural astronomical instruments** used for measuring time, predicting eclipses, tracking celestial objects, and determining the positions of planets and stars.
 
• The observatory houses the **world's largest stone sundial**, called the "Samrat Yantra."
 
• Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is one of the five such observatories built by Sawai Jai Singh II, but it is the largest and best-preserved among them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **UNESCO World Heritage Site:**

 
 
• Jantar Mantar was inscribed as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in **2010** for its cultural and scientific significance.
 
• It represents an excellent example of the scientific and cultural advancements of 18th-century India.
 
 
 
• **Astronomical Instruments:**
 
 
• Key instruments at Jantar Mantar include the Samrat Yantra (sundial), Jai Prakash Yantra (hemisphere), and Ram Yantra (altitude instruments).
 
• These instruments were designed to observe astronomical phenomena with the naked eye.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• Maharaja Sawai Jai Singh II, the founder of Jaipur, was a keen astronomer and mathematician.
 
• His interest in astronomy led to the construction of five observatories in Jaipur, Delhi, Ujjain, Mathura, and Varanasi, with Jaipur's being the most prominent.
 
 
 
• **Tourist Attraction:**
 
 
• Jantar Mantar in Jaipur is a popular tourist destination, attracting history and science enthusiasts from around the world.
 
• It is also used for educational purposes to teach astronomy and the history of science in India.

questions.question: Which of the following options in PowerPoint allows you to see all the slides at once as thumbnails?

• The **Slide Sorter View** in Microsoft PowerPoint displays all slides in a presentation as thumbnails, allowing users to easily rearrange, delete, or apply transitions between slides.
 
• This view provides a **bird's-eye view of the entire presentation**, making it easier to organize slides and review the flow of content.
 
• Slide Sorter View is **especially useful for large presentations** with numerous slides, as it enables quick identification and movement of specific slides.
 
• It can be accessed from the **View tab** on the Ribbon or by clicking on the Slide Sorter icon in the bottom-right corner of the PowerPoint interface.
 
• In this view, users can also apply **slide transitions** to multiple slides simultaneously by selecting them and using the Transitions tab.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__

__
 
• Representative elements include elements from both the **s-block** (Groups 1 and 2) and the **p-block** (Groups 13 to 18) of the periodic table.
 
• These elements are characterized by having their outermost electrons in s- or p-orbitals, which define their chemical properties.

• **p-block elements:** Found in Groups 13 to 18, p-block elements include metals, nonmetals, and metalloids, and exhibit diverse properties such as variable oxidation states and covalent bonding.
 
• **Transition elements:** These are found in the d-block (Groups 3 to 12) and are distinguished by their partially filled d-orbitals, leading to properties like variable oxidation states and the formation of colored compounds.
 
• **Periodic table structure:** The periodic table is divided into blocks based on the type of orbital being filled (s-block, p-block, d-block, and f-block). Representative elements are part of the s- and p-blocks.
 
• **Metalloids:** Some representative elements, such as silicon and boron, are classified as metalloids and exhibit properties intermediate between metals and nonmetals.

• A horizontal row in the periodic table is known as a **period.**
 
• Periods indicate the **principal energy level** or shell that the electrons occupy for a given element.
 
• There are **7 periods** in the modern periodic table, ranging from Period 1 to Period 7.
 
• As we move from left to right across a period, the **atomic number increases sequentially**, meaning the number of protons in the nucleus increases.

• **Periods:** Horizontal rows where properties change progressively across the row due to increasing atomic number.
 
 
 
• **Periodic Trends:** Trends such as atomic size, ionization energy, and electronegativity change across a period due to increasing nuclear charge.
 
• **Electron Configuration:** Elements in a period have electrons filling the same principal energy level (shell).
 
• **Periodic Table Organization:** The periodic table is based on the periodic law, which states that the properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.
 
• **Lanthanides and Actinides:** These form part of Periods 6 and 7, placed separately at the bottom of the table for better visualization.

• Cardiac muscles are striated and involuntary.
 
• They are exclusively found in the heart and are responsible for rhythmic contractions.
 
• Contractions are regulated by pacemaker cells and the autonomic nervous system.
 
 
 
• **Peristalsis**
 
 
• A wave-like motion produced by smooth muscle contractions in the gastrointestinal tract.

questions.question: The Thar Desert is classified as which of the following?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 2,

The correct answer is __**Subtropical Desert**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Thar Desert, also known as the Great Indian Desert, is classified as a **subtropical desert** due to its location and climatic conditions.
 
• It is located in the northwestern part of India and eastern Pakistan, covering an area of approximately **200,000 square kilometers**.
 
• Subtropical deserts are characterized by **high temperatures during the day**, cooler nights, and **low annual rainfall**.
 
• The Thar Desert receives an annual rainfall of less than **200 mm**, making it one of the driest regions in India.
 
• Its climate is influenced by the **Hadley cell circulation**, which creates stable, dry air masses over subtropical latitudes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Subtropical Desert Characteristics**

 
 
• Subtropical deserts are located between **20° and 30° north or south latitude**.
 
• They have **hot summers** with temperatures often exceeding 40°C.
 
• Rainfall is scarce, often occurring in brief, sporadic showers.
 
• Vegetation is sparse and adapted to drought conditions.
 
 
 
• **Geography of the Thar Desert**
 
 
• It covers parts of Rajasthan, Gujarat, Punjab, and Haryana in India and Sindh in Pakistan.
 
• The desert is home to unique sand dune formations and salt marshes like the **Rann of Kutch**.
 
 
 
• **Flora and Fauna**
 
 
• Vegetation includes drought-resistant shrubs, grasses, and **acacia trees**.
 
• Wildlife includes species like desert foxes, camels, and the endangered **Great Indian Bustard**.
 
 
 
• **Human Settlement**
 
 
• The Thar Desert is one of the most densely populated deserts in the world.
 
• Communities rely on agriculture, animal husbandry, and tourism for their livelihoods.

questions.question: "Purvang" and "Uttarang" are two sections of which of the components of Carnatic Music?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Varnam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Purvang** and **Uttarang** are two integral sections of a Varnam__, a fundamental compositional form in Carnatic music.
 
• The **Purvang** (first section) typically consists of the __Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Muktayi Swaras__, while the **Uttarang** (second section) includes the __Charanam and Charana Swaras__.
 
• Varnam serves as an introductory piece in Carnatic music concerts and is used for both __performance and practice__.
 
• It is designed to showcase the raga's essence through a combination of **melodic and rhythmic elements**.
 
• Varnams are critical for improving a musician's mastery of **raga alapana, swara singing, and rhythm**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Varnam in Carnatic Music**

 
 
• It is an important compositional form in Carnatic music with both lyrical and swara-based__ segments.
 
• There are two types of Varnams: **Tana Varnam** (focused on swaras) and **Pada Varnam** (focused on lyrical content).
 
• It serves as a warm-up for vocalists and instrumentalists due to its complexity and extensive range of notes.
 
 
 
• **Pallavi, Anupallavi, and Charanam**
 __
 
• **Pallavi:** The main thematic line of the composition, repeated throughout.
 
• **Anupallavi:** A short stanza that complements the Pallavi, often elaborating on its theme.
 
• **Charanam:** The concluding section that provides variations and deeper explorations of the raga.
 
 
 
• **Role of Swaras in Varnam**
 
 
• Swara patterns in Varnam are used for strengthening control over rhythm and melody__.
 
• Muktayi Swaras and Charana Swaras are key segments that demonstrate the raga's nuances.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Music Structure**
 __
 
• Carnatic music is deeply rooted in ragas__ (melodic frameworks) and __talas__ (rhythmic cycles).
 
• Compositions like Varnams, Kritis, and Tillanas serve as the foundation for its performance repertoire.

questions.question: The Indus Valley Civilization flourished around:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**2500-1800 BCE**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indus Valley Civilization (IVC) is one of the world's earliest urban civilizations, flourishing during the **Bronze Age (circa 2500-1800 BCE)**.
 
• It was located in the northwestern regions of South Asia, primarily in modern-day **India and Pakistan**.
 
• The civilization is known for its advanced urban planning, including **grid-pattern cities, drainage systems, and standardized weights and measures**.
 
• Major urban centers of the IVC include **Harappa, Mohenjo-Daro, Dholavira, and Lothal**.
 
• The decline of the civilization is believed to have been caused by factors such as **climate change, river shifts, and possibly invasions**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Urban Features:** Cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa featured advanced urban layouts with **well-planned streets, public baths, and granaries**.
 
• **Trade and Economy:** The Indus people were skilled traders, and evidence suggests they engaged in long-distance trade with **Mesopotamia and Central Asia**.
 
• **Script:** The civilization used an **script** comprising pictographic symbols, often inscribed on seals.
 
• **Artefacts:** Artefacts such as the **“Dancing Girl” bronze statue** and the “Priest-King” sculpture highlight their artistic and cultural achievements.
 
• **Decline:** The decline of the IVC around 1800 BCE is linked to environmental factors, including **changes in river systems (e.g., drying of the Saraswati River)**.

questions.question: In February 2025, which bank of India has announced $10 billion three-year dollar/rupee swap auction?

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, as the central bank of India, regularly conducts dollar-rupee swap auctions to manage liquidity and stabilize currency fluctuations.
 
• In February 2025, RBI announced a **$10 billion three-year dollar-rupee swap auction** aimed at enhancing liquidity management and providing stability to the foreign exchange market.
 
• Dollar-rupee swap auctions are a tool used by RBI to infuse liquidity in the Indian banking system by exchanging US dollars for Indian rupees with a promise to reverse the transaction in the future.
 
• Such auctions are critical for addressing short-term liquidity mismatches while ensuring the smooth functioning of financial markets.
 
• The move aligns with RBI's proactive measures to manage external risks and stabilize the value of the Indian rupee amidst global economic uncertainties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Dollar-Rupee Swap Explained:**

 
 
• A dollar-rupee swap is a financial transaction where RBI buys US dollars from banks in exchange for rupees with an agreement to reverse the transaction at a future date.
 
• This mechanism helps in managing both liquidity and foreign exchange reserves efficiently.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Forex Swap Auctions:**
 
 
• Forex swaps ensure adequate liquidity in the banking system and reduce volatility in currency markets.
 
• They play a crucial role in balancing the demand and supply of foreign currency in the domestic market.
 
 
 
• **RBI's Role in Monetary Policy:**
 
 
• RBI uses various monetary tools such as repo rate, reverse repo rate, and forex swaps to regulate liquidity and inflation.
 
• Forex swaps complement these tools by addressing external sector risks and stabilizing exchange rates.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Financial Markets:**
 
 
• Such auctions are closely monitored by investors and banks as they impact liquidity, interest rates, and currency exchange rates.
 
• The announcement of a $10 billion swap auction reflects RBI's commitment to maintaining financial stability amidst global economic challenges.

questions.question: The Mauryan period saw the development of which script for inscriptions?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brahmi script** was the primary script used for inscriptions during the Mauryan period, particularly in Emperor Ashoka's edicts.
 
• It is one of the oldest writing systems in South Asia and is considered the **ancestor of most modern Indian scripts**, including Devanagari, Tamil, and Bengali.
 
• Brahmi was written from **left to right**, unlike Kharosthi, which was written from right to left.
 
• The inscriptions in Brahmi during the Mauryan period were often used to disseminate **Ashoka’s messages of Dhamma (moral and ethical principles)**.
 
• Deciphered by **James Prinsep in 1837**, the Brahmi script unlocked critical insights into ancient Indian history and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kharosthi Script**

 
 
• This was another ancient script used in the northwestern parts of the Indian subcontinent, written from right to left.
 
• It was influenced by the Aramaic script and primarily used in the Gandhara region (modern-day Pakistan and Afghanistan).
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Edicts**
 
 
• The Mauryan Emperor Ashoka issued a series of inscriptions on rocks and pillars to propagate his policy of Dhamma.
 
• These edicts were written in Brahmi, Kharosthi, and other regional scripts depending on the location of the inscriptions.
 
 
 
• **Grantha Script**
 
 
• Grantha script was used in South India, primarily for writing Sanskrit texts.
 
• It developed much later and is not associated with the Mauryan period.
 
 
 
• **Pali and Prakrit**
 
 
• Pali and Prakrit are ancient languages, not scripts, often used in Buddhist and Jain texts.
 
• Many of Ashoka's inscriptions were written in Prakrit, but they used the Brahmi script.
 
 
 
• **James Prinsep’s Contribution**
 
 
• James Prinsep was a British scholar who deciphered the Brahmi and Kharosthi scripts in 1837.
 
• His work enabled historians to understand the Mauryan inscriptions and reconstruct India's ancient history.

questions.question: In the context of computer hardware components, what is the primary function of ROM?

options.text: It holds essential firmware required for booting the system
It physically supports all internal hardware modules
It stores temporary data used during system processing
It executes programs and handles arithmetic operations.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 1,

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• ROM (Read-Only Memory) is a type of non-volatile memory that retains its contents even when the computer is powered off.
 
• The primary function of ROM is to store essential firmware, such as the BIOS, which is required for booting the system.
 
• Firmware stored in ROM is hardcoded during manufacturing and is not meant to be modified by regular users.
 
• Unlike RAM, ROM does not lose its data when the system is shut down, making it critical for initializing hardware components during startup.
 
• ROM is used in various devices, including computers, smartphones, embedded systems, and gaming consoles, to provide stable and reliable operation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **BIOS (Basic Input/Output System)**

 
 
• The BIOS is firmware stored in ROM and is responsible for initializing hardware during the boot process.
 
• It provides an interface for the operating system to interact with the hardware components.
 
• Modern systems may use UEFI (Unified Extensible Firmware Interface) instead of traditional BIOS.
 
 
 
• **Non-Volatile Memory**
 
 
• Non-volatile memory retains data even when the power supply is cut off.
 
• Examples include ROM, EEPROM, and Flash memory.
 
• It is essential for storing permanent data or firmware.
 
 
 
• **EEPROM (Electrically Erasable Programmable Read-Only Memory)**
 
 
• EEPROM is a type of ROM that can be erased and reprogrammed electrically.
 
• It allows limited updates to firmware or settings stored on the device.
 
 
 
• **RAM vs ROM**
 
 
• RAM (Random Access Memory) is volatile and used for temporary data storage during system processing.
 
• ROM is non-volatile and stores permanent data, such as firmware.
 
• Both are essential for system operation but serve different purposes.

questions.question: When was the designation of the Governor General in India promoted as a Viceroy or Crown's representative?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Year 1858**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The title of **Governor-General of India** was replaced by the title of **Viceroy of India in 1858**, following the Government of India Act 1858.
 
• This change marked the formal transfer of authority from the **East India Company to the British Crown**, after the events of the Revolt of 1857 (also called the First War of Independence).
 
• The Viceroy acted as the **direct representative of the British Crown** and was responsible for administering India on behalf of the monarch.
 
• Lord Canning, who was the last Governor-General of India, became the **first Viceroy of India** in 1858.
 
• The **Government of India Act 1858** was a significant legislative change that centralized governance under the Crown, ending the dual control system of the East India Company.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Revolt of 1857:**

 
 
• Also known as India's First War of Independence, it was a major uprising against the rule of the British East India Company.
 
• The revolt led to significant political changes, including the abolition of the East India Company's rule in India.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act 1858:**
 
 
• This act abolished the East India Company's authority and transferred governance directly to the British Crown.
 
• A new office called the "Secretary of State for India" was created to oversee Indian administration from Britain.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Viceroy:**
 
 
• The Viceroy served as the head of the colonial administration in India.
 
• He was responsible for implementing policies and laws on behalf of the British Crown.
 
 
 
• **Lord Canning:**
 
 
• He was the last Governor-General of India under the East India Company.
 
• He became the first Viceroy of India after the Government of India Act 1858 came into effect.
 
 
 
• **Significance of 1858:**
 
 
• The transition symbolized the beginning of the British Crown’s direct rule over India, which lasted until Indian independence in 1947.

questions.question: Which of the following rivers originates in the Western Ghats?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Krishna**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Krishna River originates in the **Western Ghats** near Mahabaleshwar in the state of Maharashtra, India.
 
• It is one of the longest rivers in India, with a total length of approximately **1,400 km**, flowing through Maharashtra, Karnataka, Telangana, and Andhra Pradesh.
 
• The river flows eastward and empties into the Bay of Bengal, supporting agriculture and irrigation along its course.
 
• Key tributaries of the Krishna River include the **Tungabhadra, Koyna, and Bhima Rivers**, among others.
 
• The Krishna River basin is known for its fertile lands and is a vital water source for millions in South India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Western Ghats**

 
 
• The Western Ghats are a mountain range that runs parallel to the western coast of India, known for their biodiversity and ecological significance.
 
• They are a UNESCO World Heritage Site and a major source of many important rivers in peninsular India.
 
 
 
• **Major Rivers Originating in the Western Ghats:**
 
 
• Besides Krishna, other important rivers originating from the Western Ghats include the Godavari, Kaveri, and Periyar.
 
• These rivers are crucial for irrigation, drinking water, and hydroelectric power generation in the southern states of India.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Krishna River:**
 
 
• The Krishna River is essential for agriculture, providing irrigation to large areas in the Deccan Plateau.
 
• It supports several major dams and irrigation projects, such as the Nagarjuna Sagar Dam and the Srisailam Dam.
 
 
 
• **Ecological Concerns:**
 
 
• Like many rivers in India, the Krishna River faces challenges such as pollution, over-extraction of water, and reduced flow due to climate change.
 
• Efforts are being made to conserve and sustainably manage the river and its basin.
